sentences.text: 3. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the State opposed the application for grant of bail.
It is submitted that offence is serious in nature.

4. Heard the counsel for the parties.
5.
As per arguments of counsel for the applicant, applicant was under influence of his master and therefore, he has acted as per his instructions.
Said fact is also reflected in case diary.
6 . Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on the merits of the case, bail application filed by the applicant is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his regular appearance before Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of trial on aforesaid conditions.

7. The applicant shall also abide by the conditions enumeration under Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is second application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.401/2023, registered at Police Station T.T.
Nagar, District Bhopal (MP) for the offence under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.
As per arguments of counsel for the applicant, applicant was under influence of his master and therefore, he has acted as per his instructions.
Said fact is also reflected in case diary.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
2. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that applicant is servant of complainant and illiterate person.
He was taken to Registrar Office by main accused persons representing him that he will be required as witness but he was used as an imposter for selling the land in question.
Applicant is in jail for quite some time.
In these circumstances, he prayed that applicant be released on bail.
